heading: INT. ARBITRATION ROOM, OLD COURTHOUSE - DAY

units.text: INT. ARBITRATION ROOM, OLD COURTHOUSE - DAY
Oak panels.
A tall window.
A radiator that knocks.
JUDGE ABERNATHY, 60s, bifocals on a chain, presides.
MR. OKAFOR, 40s, sharp navy suit, and MR. LINDGREN, 40s, charcoal suit, glare across a narrow table.
MS. TSUKAMOTO, 30s, the court reporter, hovers over a steno machine.
BAILIFF DUFFY, 50s, leans against the door.
Mr. Okafor, you may proceed.
units.name: JUDGE ABERNATHY

units.text: Thank you, Your Honor. Mr. Lindgren's client signed on the fourth. He knew what he was signing.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: He did not. He thought it was the lease.
units.name: LINDGREN

units.text: Then he should have read it.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: He did. Twice. And he still didn't know what he was signing.
units.name: LINDGREN

units.text: Mr. Lindgren. Mr. Okafor. Please.
units.name: JUDGE ABERNATHY

units.text: Your Honor, he is stalling because he has no evidence.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: He is shouting because he has no case.
units.name: LINDGREN

units.text: The radiator knocks.
Everyone looks at it.
That's been happening since Monday, Judge.
units.name: DUFFY

units.text: Thank you, Duffy.
units.name: JUDGE ABERNATHY

units.text: Your Honor, may I ask counsel to speak one at a time?
units.name: TSUKAMOTO

units.text: You may. And you shall.
units.name: JUDGE ABERNATHY

units.text: A beat.
Okafor pulls a paper from his folder.
Exhibit nine. A signature, notarized, dated the fourth.
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: That is not my client's signature.
units.name: LINDGREN

units.text: What?
units.name: OKAFOR

units.text: That is yours.
units.name: LINDGREN

units.text: Okafor looks at the page.
His face drains.
The radiator knocks again, softly.
Mr. Okafor, would you care to explain?
units.name: JUDGE ABERNATHY

units.text: Okafor laughs.
Short.
Then longer.
Your Honor, I may have grabbed the wrong folder.
units.name: OKAFOR
